rows.goal: Sleep a chosen number of hours, from now or from a later bedtime | The Sleep dialog (src/ui/shell/TimeControls.tsx SleepDialog, run('life.sleep', { hours }) at :175; it never sends startAt) sends life.sleep. The command refuses: hours that aren't a number ('Say how long to sleep.', life.ts:368); a start that isn't finite (:371), is in the past, or is more than a day ahead (:373); and a start inside a kept commitment, through occupiedAt (:374, 'You’re at X until Y.'). It clamps hours to [SHORTEST_SLEEP, 16], stamps lastSleptAt as the wake when the night is booked, advances to the start, reads sleepQuality (nightParts: stress, the sleepQuality knob, a late hour), sets awakeSince to the wake, and advances to the wake while the world runs. Then applySleep moves energy, sleepDebt, stress, condition, morale and nourishment, and wokeWithDebt is set (:409). If requiresPlayer items fall inside the night it posts 'You Slept Through N Commitment(s)' (:414-423). Downstream: a commitment slept through is missed (the PLAN_KIND asleep branch; school classes and sessions through present(); appointments through presentForCare; rehearsals and coursework through awakeSince); sleepAlone gives no second night; readiness feeds focusOf; the waking drain reads wokeWithDebt.

rows.goal: Work Out from the Look After menu. Refused: in hospital; at energy < 25 ('too tired'); when injured (trainingRefusal); with the flu; during a kept commitment; on a clash within its 60 minutes; for a repeated actionId. Once the hour is lived, trainingAt (read as the hour ends) chooses run (1.1) or indoors (1). A second workout the same day builds 0.5^repeats. Fitness rises by workoutBuilds*builds, up to the age's ceiling. Energy falls by workoutCosts, nourishment by 6, hygiene by 20*hygieneDrift, stress by 8*stressRecovery; morale rises by 3*swing. The workout records stamina development and development.workout.at, adds to body.extra (exerts), and rolls an injury (mayHurt), which can bring a bill. Downstream: settleTheBody holds fitness three days; mendsTo turns fitness into condition; stamina feeds a task's consistency; trainingRefusal reads the injury; the health bill.

rows.goal: Choose how the day’s spending is paid, and set up standing orders and scheduled payments | From How You Pay (button BankPayments.tsx:113, run at :47) the player sets an amount and a day of the month into one of their own open easy-access savings accounts. The command validates the target (own, open, savings, not a term deposit), the amount and the day, records the order in person.payments.standingOrders and schedules bank.standing_order for the next such day at 9 AM. Each month the handler moves the amount from the account it pays from (orderSource: the primary when first read, pinned on a change of primary) into the savings: at once at the same bank, or out on the day and in on the sending bank's days at another bank. It skips the month with 'A Standing Order Didn't Go' when the account is short, closed, dormant, closing, blocked by a switch or a term deposit, then re-arms for the next month. armPayments re-arms orders when a save loads.

Refused too for a ChexSystems report, collections, no photo ID, an overdraft, or a switch already under way.

rows.goal: Move money between your own accounts, and open or close a savings account | Move Money moves an amount between two of the holder's own current or easy-access savings accounts. It's refused past the balance, for the same account, from an account a switch left in debt, when dormant, past Germany's allowance, past room after the withdrawal fee, or when closing. rows.goal: Apply for a card, pay it, set its autopay and statement day, ask for a limit or help, and close it | Apply (BankCard) applies for a card at a bank in the country you bank in, with an optional balance transfer. It's refused while one is on its way, for a bank with no card, for another country, and for a bank whose card is already held. The application costs 5 points (a hard inquiry), approved or not. It's declined, with the reason in a notice, for a score under 620, a debt in collections, or no means. rows.goal: On its day the handler (credit.ts:702-790) does the following. It charges cash-advance interest, offers' interest and fees, and the cycle's rewards; charges carried interest and trailing interest; refunds a US credit balance after six months; charges the yearly fee once in the opening month (first-year US cap); charges an over-limit fee at most three cycles. It records persistent debt (GB), sets statementBalance and resets paidSinceStatement. Every six months it raises the limit by a fifth for a clean record unless the holder said never. It records what the statement said, schedules the due date or reports the month on time, closes a closing card once paid, and schedules the next statement.

rows.goal: Apply for or renew a passport, get a state ID card, and report, police-report and replace a lost document | Papers > Passport And ID > Your ID 'Get Non-Driver Identification Card' runs documents.apply_idcard. idCardRefusal gates it: SLATE issues a card where they live; a citizen-only card; age; Ireland's book; refused while holding a license from there in force ('It serves as your ID'); for a non-citizen at a US counter, in status, an F-1 at school or a US permit (OPT) in force, and a Social Security number held, with three refusal wordings for a number on its way, a student sent to Papers, and anyone else. It charges the card's fee from the bank and pushes an idcard. For a citizen it is valid at once, with a 6-year term in CT. rows.goal: Claim unemployment, apply for assistance, and register for Canada’s EI | Papers > Benefits 'File A Claim' runs benefits.claim. The button is hidden while studying, without permission to work, or with a short base period. Britain, Ireland and Mexico City route to their own claims. In the US the state is the base-period wages' state, or else the home state. The claim is refused when one is open, for a CT full-time student (CGS 31-235(b)), and for a non-citizen without a US work permit (FUTA). The monetary test runs on the basic or alternate base period. The command records the claim (CT has no waiting week) and schedules BENEFIT_WEEK_KIND for the next Sunday at 8 PM. Each week checks availability, reduces the benefit by the week's work (workedBetween -> weekBenefit), applies the waiting week, posts to the payee account and records the benefit through recordBenefit (yearOf().unemployment, the unearned kind). The claim closes at maxTotal or after a year. The return counts it as income.

rows.goal: File each year’s tax return, amend it, and pay what’s owed to the IRS and to a state | 'File It' on the Returns tab, or the decision 'Your <year> Tax Return' made each February, runs tax.file. It does these things: refigures the year (figuresFor); sets filedAt and the late penalty; resolves the decision; files each state's side; then the IRS side. That side is a refund scheduled 21 days on (plus ITIN weeks for a 1040-NR without an SSN), or the balance with penalty and interest paid from the bank, or, if the bank can't pay, owed with collection begun. It also cancels a pending substitute return. A substitute already assessed is reconsidered instead.

rows.goal: US_STATUS_KIND is armed at createSave and loadSave, and again whenever a program or permit changes. When permission has run out and the grace has begun, it sends the decision 'Your US Status Is Ending' (with Apply For OPT where open). rows.goal: The IRS's collection on an owed return. It holds while a plan is pending, active or in default. Otherwise it accrues, then sends four notices (CP501, CP503, CP504, LT11) five weeks apart, filing the federal lien at the LT11 when $10,000 or more is owed. Thirty days later it levies what the bank accounts hold, up to what's owed (drawFromBank, applyPayment 'levy'), and while anything is still owed it levies again every 91 days. Paid in full, the pending notices are cancelled.

rows.goal: Answer what a classmate brings in class, and make amends | Answering a classmate's moment (ClassMoments), refused if none, lapsed, answered, not a choice, a disagreement on finished work, help away/not free, a study evening passed/clashing. Disagreement: hold (trust/bond by whether the text supports theirs over yours; a.readsApart), theirs (answers[q] = theirs, readsApart cleared, trust +2 bond +1), both (tryBoth, trust +3 bond +1). Study: yes books STUDY_KIND on the chosen shared scene; no remembered (two stop them asking). Help: 45 minutes, trust +4 bond +3 (they ask in turn). Apology: bond +/-2. Boundary: respect (accepted, trust +2, lifts after 2 kept) or argue (pushed back, trust -3 bond -4, lifts after 4). Read by classMoment's candidates, keptWith, askRefusal's boundary decline, interpretationOf, partnerReadOf's agreement, and a kept rehearsal clearing tryBoth.

Otherwise the read takes 120 minutes (60 for a short play or monologue; 0.75 of that read again) and spends energy. If fresh (first read, or 30+ days since the last) it grows script and imagination through ordinary(), recorded. rows.goal: Each School/Rep call cast() books (rehearsal, performance, understudy run-through, night on call) fires on the clock. Off sick or on the day called in sick: excused (a rehearsal's stage still a gap via callMissed; an excused last performance still closes the run). Otherwise tally.calls/answered; a rehearsal answered moves the process (callAnswered, a craft note at a work-through) and grows craft (rehearse); a performance played counts performed, nerves, friends' morale, is judged by reckonNight as the craft stood (band, work record, delivery, noteRun, listening, genres, nights, the night together's mood where classmates are cast, presence on a remarkable night, material) and then grows craft (playNight); the last night closes the run (closeRun: 'run' milestone, the director's note naming what held the nights back, reflect). Missed unexcused: rehearsal -> callMissed + missedCallsOut (castable false); performance -> noteRun 'missed', breach, and closeRun on the last. Downstream: evaluate (attendance, work nights, breaches), cast()/readRuns lastWork.delivery, the casting pool.

rows.goal: Take a leave of absence, call it off, appeal one the dean imposed, come back from it, or withdraw | Ask on the leave panel (StudyPlanPanels.tsx:134) sends school.request_leave. leaveRefusal gates it: one request at a time, the reason must match the kind, no professional reason, a physician's recommendation for a medical leave, and for a personal leave a term completed, the student current with requirements and not on an F-1. leaveLengths sets the length. It leaves school.leave pending and schedules LEAVE_DECIDE_KIND for five working days, or for the next term's start if that comes first. The decision refuses a personal leave that is no longer current ('Your Leave Is Refused') or grants it. When granted, startLeave withdraws the term's courses, moves offset and classOf, ends classes, castings and a Cabaret show, returns the living aid to the Yale account on the rebate schedule, ends the student cover (or keeps a medical leave's Affiliate cover) and extends an F-1's I-20. If no notice is given, LEAVE_NOTICE_KIND dismisses the student.

A Fail is told after the evaluation settles the standing (tellFails, from 2026-10-15) and offered the year’s end only where a repeat can still be asked: not where that evaluation dismissed or withheld, not in an additional term, and not where the repeat would pass nine semesters counted as the year’s end will count them (repeatRoom), which after any repeat granted is every year, the repeated one included; a Permanent Incomplete likewise, and not where the degree waits on it (scope-school, played: the repeated year’s Permanent Incomplete, and a second fall’s Fail after a first year’s repeat, its year’s end refused “Repeating would make 10 semesters…”). The decision’s refusals (past nine, or a disqualification the faculty didn’t keep them through) are guards no request the asking takes reaches, tested as guards (scope-school GUARD:). rows.goal: A bank closing an idle German account at zero (closedByBank and the dormancy/idle path): it can go negative from fees on closing; make the bank's own close settle consistently; closure can't erase debt or strand money; closed accounts stop all recurring processing.
rows.entry: systems/bankmoves.ts closedByBank, closeNow, closeRefusal; systems/lending.ts closeForOverdraft, completeSwitch; systems/banking.ts settleFees, closingFeesOf, dropPaymentsFor; systems/abroad.ts homeCloses; systems/accountlife.ts cancelRefusal, bank.cancel_new; systems/routing.ts redirectAway; content/guide/money.ts bank.other-banks, bank.borrowing, bank.upkeep; content/tutorial.ts the bank chapter's overdraft sentence
rows.preconditions: BGB § 675h(2): a payment service provider ends a framework contract on at least two months' notice; § 675h(3): on termination, regularly charged fees are owed pro rata up to the end of the contract (dejure.org text, read 2026-10-16; gesetze-im-internet.de refused the fetch with 503). So fees accrued to the closing are owed, not forgiven, and a balance can't be manufactured where there is none to take them from. The project's own rule (CLAUDE.md, the ledger law; brief section 7): every movement a balanced posting, funds never vanish or duplicate, a closure can't strand money or erase a debt. SLATE's existing rule for a customer's close (bankmoves.ts closeRefusal:282-307, accountlife.ts cancelRefusal:237-261): the bank closes an overdrawn account only once that's paid.
rows.reads: No German bank reaches the bank's own close at zero: closedByBank (bankmoves.ts:333-340) runs only from the day's check at bankmoves.ts:420-438, which reads OPENING (content/bankopening.ts:44-84), and only Citi (closesAtZeroAfterDays 90) and Capital One (fundWithinDays 60) carry those rules. Germany has no unclaimed-money law (content/accountlife.ts UNCLAIMED.DE has no years), so idleAccounts (accountlife.ts:609-646) never closes a German account, and dormancy (accountlife.ts:616-619) blocks without closing. So the defect named is latent: closedByBank checks `balance !== 0` before closeNow (bankmoves.ts:310-326), which then settles interest (settleInterest, banking.ts:508) and fees (settleFees, banking.ts:492-500, Germany's quarter only); with no remainderTo, interest settled would stay on a closed account (stranded), and fees would leave a closed account negative with nothing pursuing it (leftOverdrawn, lending.ts:937-953, skips closed accounts). Reproduced only with a bank given a zero-close rule in a test (TEST SETUP). The German bank's own close that does happen is the overdraft's (closeForOverdraft, lending.ts:955-1054): reproduced on a Berlin quickSave (probe, Commerzbank primary, a Deutsche Bank AktivKonto €100 under from 5 January 2026): charged off on 7 March at €101.97 with feesDue €13.80 (January's and February's €6.90) left on the closed account and never charged, and March's fee and the overdraft interest built since 1 March (odAccrued) dropped too. Played the same way at a home account abroad (a German home bank's AktivKonto emptied to Chase, its €6.90 overdrawing it).
rows.decisions: closedByBank: work out what closing would settle (interest net of tax, the fees closing charges, the overdraft interest built) before closing; close only where that leaves nothing owed, and send anything it leaves (interest) to the current account kept elsewhere by the bank's own payment, never stranded; where closing would leave it owing, don't close: the charges post at their regular closing and the account is pursued as any overdrawn one (the 60 days, closeForOverdraft), as the customer's Close It refuses it. closeForOverdraft: settle the overdraft interest built and, on each account it closes, Germany's quarter of fees before the set-off, so they're set off or charged off with the rest, never dropped; the quiet re-banking after a charge-off doesn't settle them a second time or move a negative to the new bank. Scheduled payments and standing orders into an account it closes dropped (dropPaymentsFor), as every other close does. Recurring processing on a closed account checked one by one (interest, fees, the abroad fee, statements, round-ups, alerts, standing orders) and tested.
rows.validation: closedByBank's settlement: necessary defensive guard (no current journey gives it anything to settle). closeForOverdraft's dropped fees and overdraft interest: required reachable behavior (a played home account abroad reaches it).
rows.changes: closedByBank works out what closing settles first: owed more than it holds it isn’t closed (the charges post when due, and the overdrawn path pursues them); what it leaves goes to the primary by the bank’s own payment; a standing order from it ends, said in the notice; closeForOverdraft settles the overdraft interest built since the 1st on every account at the bank and the fees of each account it closes before the set-off, and every account’s fees on a charge-off, so the debt is all of it to the day; completeSwitch’s quiet re-banking after a charge-off doesn’t settle the fees again

rows.preconditions: Where the country's rule returns what each side received on a withdrawal (Directive 2002/65/EC art. 7(4)-(5); BGB § 355(3); Mexico's LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1, as cited in accountlife.ts:131-157), interest already paid out of the term goes back on canceling it, with its tax, and off the year's income. The project's rules: never fabricate a transaction or double-count income; an older save keeps its legitimate balances and history; a one-time step on opening is named in SaveUniverse.opened so a reload never repeats it (index.ts:279-286, 327-334, followTheCover).
rows.reads: Since a4d05745 (2026-10-15) bank.take_term_interest posts a zero posting against the term (accountlife.ts:484-501) and interestPaidSince (accountlife.ts:176-179) finds a term's taken interest by it. A build before that (git show a4d05745^:src/engine/systems/accountlife.ts:294-309) posted only the primary account (net), the Interest income line (gross) and Tax On Interest, memo “Interest: <term name>”, a name every term at the bank shares. So in an older save interestBackOf (accountlife.ts:192-199) finds nothing: cancelRefusal doesn't count it and bank.cancel_new (accountlife.ts:549-557) returns none of it; the interest stays paid and on the year's income. Reproduced by writing a save as that build wrote it (the zero posting taken off, `opened` without the new step) and canceling. The records an older save holds that tell same-named terms apart: the term's own id, opening instant, fixed rate, balance and accrued (what's left built after each take, accountlife.ts:498), and the clock's day ends (life.ts:350-358): the interest a term builds is its balance × rate / 365 at each day's end (lending.ts:1162), so each take was the whole cents of what it had built since opening less what was taken before, and what's left is term.accrued. A transaction's memo, date, gross, net and the account it went into are kept; nothing else names the term.
rows.decisions: A one-time step on opening (`findTermInterest`, named in SaveUniverse.opened): for each open term deposit still in its cooling-off, its bank letting interest be taken during the term, the untagged “Interest: <name>” transactions into its holder's account from its opening on are the candidates; the term's own accrual is replayed day end by day end from its opening (its balance × its rate / 365, each candidate taken where it equals the whole cents built then), and only a set of candidates that reproduces the term's stored accrued exactly is taken as its own, the earliest where two fit, and none taken by another term. Recorded on the term as the transactions' ids; interestPaidSince reads them beside the tag. Where no set fits, nothing is attributed: the interest stays as the build that paid it left it (that build never returned it), never taken back from a term that may not have paid it. The guide says what it does.
rows.changes: findTermInterest, a one-time step on opening named in SaveUniverse.opened: each term’s accrual replayed from its opening (balance × rate / 365 at each day’s end, in the build’s order), the untagged “Interest: <name>” takes since it opened that reproduce its stored accrued exactly kept on it as untaggedTakes (oldest term first, a take never given twice); interestPaidSince reads them

rows.preconditions: The project's own rule (CLAUDE.md, rule 7; the owner's brief of this pass, section 14: 'no aggregate that conceals unfinished behavior', denominators reported): the totals say apart how each row is evidenced. Player journeys (a gate test reaches the action as a player does), retained engine verification (the action is beyond any current player and its engine is tested on labelled fixtures: the 9 bank and 5 tax rows, Unresolved), documentation and static checks (a claim about the repository's own text, tested against that text), and deferred scope (16). Legacy (3) and informational (8) rows fit none of the four honestly, so each keeps a class of its own named for its status rather than being forced into one of the four.
rows.reads: No row carries a class. tools/coverage.mjs:93-99 holds a row verified on any command or render test (HOLDS) and counts statuses only (:249, :404-411). Evidence kinds are recorded by the rounds: docs/verification/pipeline/scope-fold.cjs:12 `kindOf` takes a kind naming render or clock before fixture, so 51 tests in 22 rows titled FIXTURE (London, Berlin, Paris, Toronto lives, a LIFE FIXTURE) or GUARD are recorded as render or command (the earlier rounds recorded the kind they named) (reproduced: of bank.cancel_new's 18 tests, 16 are FIXTURE-titled and recorded render), and merge-review.cjs:42 maps them through KIND unchanged; so no bank row's after.tests holds a fixture, and a FIXTURE test counts toward `holding` (coverage.mjs:96-99). Every change is a posting or a bill of its own: nothing already on a statement is rewritten'; and at 1530: 'What the plan paid of the bill follows: nothing where the cover now reads none'. The house standard: 'A ledger balance is never a number somebody typed. It is the sum of postings.' The owner's brief §9 (no duplicate processing, no contradictory statuses) and this pass's item: patient + insurer = price; never double-charges; never duplicates a payment; historical bills stand; say what repricing may change and when. The plan rules: a care's price to a plan is planPrice (CARE.price grown by the medical price index); a plan pays price − share where it pays (careFor, health.ts:1479-1482): not for a Yale Health member's visit outside its Health Center (outsideItsPractice), not for restricted scope's non-hospital care, nothing while a claim stands denied.
rows.reads: health.ts:1514-1546. Reproduced on a fixture (probe/health/reprice.ts, run 2026-10-16, git-ignored): (a) a Yale Health emergency on 2 September 2026, its bill m1 $50.00 with covered {price $3,323.84, planPaid $3,273.84}, repriced as uninsured (cover canceled back to 1 August): Connecticut's charity takes the uninsured price to $0 for that income, so m1 is rewritten in place to amount $0.00, paid: true (Papers says Settled for a bill nobody paid), planPaid $0.00, with no word on the bill of the charity or the change; the issued bill's figures are gone (1530-1532, 1541). (b) An uninsured emergency on 10 September (no bill: charity free), then covered back by Yale Health: a new bill m2 of $50.00 with no plan part at all: the plan's $3,273.84 is written nowhere, so patient + insurer = $50.00 against a $3,323.84 price (1532 runs only where the bill already had `covered`). (c) The plan part is set from `planOf` (a plan exists) rather than whether the plan pays this care (outside its practice, restricted scope, a standing denial), and is skipped altogether when the share is unchanged (1527 continues before 1532). (d) Found on the way: a credit on care whose bill went to medical debt is refunded to the bank (1540-1542, `open` excludes inDebt) while the debt for the same care stands: paid twice over, once in cash and once owed.
rows.decisions: Decided: a bill as issued stands. repriceCare never writes an existing bill's plan part, and never changes a bill paid or in debt. Each care event it changes gets one adjustment line of its own (a MedicalBill naming the bill it adjusts): more owed is billed on it and due in 30 days, as now; less owed is its credit, which comes off the open original's balance first (recorded on the original as `credited`, so its issued share stays readable and Papers says Credited), then off the medical debt where the original went to debt, then back to the bank. The plan's part follows the cover now: what the plan pays now (price − share where a plan pays this care now, 0 where none does) less what the lines already show for it, written on the adjustment line as the plan's change (negative where the plan takes back). The care log keeps each event's plan part. So for every care, the patient's lines (issued less credited and credits) sum to its share now, and the plan's lines sum to the plan's part now: patient + insurer = the price where the cover pays it. rows.goal: Whether a nonresident-alien F-1 student qualifies for advance premium tax credits in 2026; what the engine should do in 2026 (the marketplace's credit, Covered Connecticut's dependence on it)
rows.entry: taxreturn.figuresFor (credit); health.creditStatus; Papers The Marketplace text; guide papers.health-cover
rows.preconditions: ENACTED (2026): an applicable taxpayer's household income at 100–400% (26 USC 36B(c)(1)(A)), filing jointly if married (36B(c)(1)(C)); a month of coverage counts only while lawfully present (36B(e)), which before §71301 took effect included nonimmigrant status (45 CFR 155.20 'lawfully present' (2): 'a valid nonimmigrant status, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)'; an F-1 is 1101(a)(15)(F)). Nothing excludes a nonresident alien: 26 CFR 1.36B-2(b) has no such rule (law.cornell.edu, read 2026-10-16); IRS Pub. 974 (2025): "You must file Form 8962 with your income tax return (Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR)" when taking the PTC; Instructions for Form 1040-NR (2025): exceptions only for dependents, for the spouse's advance payments, and for a married 1040-NR filer (irs.gov, read 2026-10-16). The marketplace: 45 CFR 155.305(a)(1) and (f)(1) (read 2026-10-16). FROM 2027: only an 'eligible alien' (36B(e)(2)(B) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §71301, taxable years after 31 December 2026; 45 CFR 155.305(f)(1)(ii)(C)), which an F-1 student isn't. So in 2026 an unmarried F-1 student in status, not eligible for Yale Health or other minimum essential coverage, at 100–400%, qualifies for APTC and the PTC on Form 1040-NR; from 2027 she doesn't. SLATE's simulation: no advance payments are modeled; the whole premium is paid and the credit is taken on the return (health.ts header), and SLATE's lives are unmarried.
rows.reads: Covered Connecticut (which needs APTC eligibility) reads creditStatus, true for anybody lawfully present before 2027 (health.ts:357-360): right. But the return gives no credit to a nonresident alien at all (taxreturn.ts:1034-1035: 'A nonresident alien isn't an applicable taxpayer for the premium tax credit, which the 1040-NR doesn't carry'): false by Pub. 974 and the 1040-NR instructions, and contradictory with Covered Connecticut, which SLATE gives her in 2026 as eligible for that very credit. It also reads no status for 2027 (an F-1's premiums in 2027 would get the credit as a resident's would, were she not a nonresident). Reproduced by reading figuresFor: credit = 0 whenever nra.

rows.goal: `repeatRoom`’s leave branch (src/engine/systems/school.ts)
rows.entry: courserecord.ts INCOMPLETE_DUE_KIND, tellFails, repeatOpen; leave.ts repeatRefusal, withRepeat, startLeave, leaveLengths; StudyPlanPanels.tsx RepeatPanel; the notices
rows.preconditions: The Permanent Incomplete and Fail notices offer the year’s end only where `repeatRefusal` would grant it (the project’s own rule since 2026-10-15, courserecord.ts:153-162); the count is the Bulletin’s nine semesters (Yale Bulletin, David Geffen School of Drama 2026–2027 (https://bulletin.yale.edu/sites/default/files/david-geffen-school-of-drama-2026-2027.pdf, PDF created 11 August 2026, read 2026-10-16), p.194: “students must complete the degree requirements within nine semesters”) under SLATE’s repeat (SLATE’s faculty model: the Bulletin has no rule for repeating). On a leave the Bulletin lets a student complete outstanding work in courses for which extensions have been granted (p.158, item 5).
rows.reads: school.ts:2950-2957: on a leave under way, next = firstTerm − (offset − (returnTerm − firstTerm)), the program term taken again on return; otherwise academicTerm(termsBegun − 1) + 1. Only INCOMPLETE_DUE_KIND reaches it on a leave (kept() keeps it, leave.ts:160; an evaluation is called off on a leave, so tellFails never runs on one). Reproduced 2026-10-16 (probe, seed rr-lv1): Acting I called in sick eleven times in Fall Term 2026 (TEST SETUP: the flu) leaves four Incompletes due Sunday 10 January 2027 at five; a medical leave asked Monday 14 December begins with Spring Term 2027 (4 January); each Incomplete extended once to Tuesday 9 February 2027 at five; on that day, on the leave, each becomes Permanent, its notice offering the year’s end; back for Spring Term 2028 and registered, at its evaluation of Friday 28 April 2028 `repeatRefusal` says nothing, and the repeat asked is granted for the four. Worked by hand: the branch counts 1 enrolled + the year’s 2 again + 4 after + (2 − 1) still to take = 8; without it next is academicTerm(1) + 1 = 0 and the count 9: both within nine. `leaveLengths` grants only two-term leaves while every year of the curriculum has year-long courses, so the branch counts 8 + 2 per repeat granted and the other path 9 + 2 per repeat: the same side of nine in every reachable state. It decides only for a three-term leave (count 8 against 10), which the Bulletin allows (p.158) and `leaveLengths` would grant for a curriculum of one-term courses.
rows.decisions: Play the preferred journey through the commands and the clock and assert the notices against `repeatRefusal` and the Standing tab at the year’s end; play a twin that makes the extended Incomplete up on the leave (p.158 item 5). Mutation-check the branch: removed, the played journey still passes (the branch decides nothing reachable, recorded); a GUARD test on a three-term leave (TEST SETUP: the leave’s length set to three before it begins, which `leaveLengths` refuses today) kills it. Keep the branch with a dated comment saying why.

rows.goal: IRS correspondence arriving before the payment due date after an early filing (taxreturn.ts armCollection / nextNotice, COLLECTION.noticeWeeks after filing); Connecticut's equivalent
rows.entry: src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts (nextNotice, tax.file, armCollection, resumeCollection, endPlan, TAX_NOTICE_KIND handler); src/engine/content/guide/taxes.ts (taxes.return later, taxes.pay short and later, IRS_LEVY_DAYS); src/engine/content/tutorial.ts (the taxes sentence); src/ui/workspaces/PapersWorkspace.tsx (Returns fine print); tests/evidence-g17-papers.test.ts, tests/liens-and-arrangements.test.ts, tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts (assertions that encode the from-filing count)
rows.preconditions: Tax shown on a return is due at the time fixed for filing it, without assessment or notice and demand (IRC 6151(a), read at law.cornell.edu 2026-10-16). Notice and demand follows an assessment, within 60 days of it (IRC 6303(a)); a levy is lawful only once the tax is unpaid 10 days after notice and demand (6331(a)) and after 30 days' written notice of intent (6331(d)(2)). Interest and the failure-to-pay penalty run only from the due date (6601(a), 6651(a)(2)). The IRS's published sequence is a first bill (CP14, 'If you owe taxes, we will send you a bill. This is your first bill for tax due'), at least one more bill, a final bill, then collection (IRS Publication 594, Rev. 1-2026, read 2026-10-16); the IRM puts the assessment (23C) date and the first notice date on the Monday of the third week after Master File posting (IRM 3.30.123.5.5, read 2026-10-16). So a balance-due bill (CP14) after processing is valid for a return filed early, naming the due date; a reminder that the balance is overdue (CP501 'you still owe it, with the interest and penalty since'), a second reminder (CP503), a notice of intent to levy (CP504) or a final notice (LT11) before the due date is premature. Whether the IRS holds an early return's CP14 until the due date wasn't found (uncertainty recorded). Connecticut: a tax 'due and unpaid' (Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-734) is collected on failure to pay 'within thirty days of its due date' (12-35(a)(2), (a)(3)), with notice 'not less than thirty days before the day the warrant is to be issued' for a bank account (12-35(b)(1)); read at codes.findlaw.com 2026-10-16.
rows.reads: Reproduced 2026-10-16 (probe/tax/repro-notice.ts, the Scraping family's played life, seed r3-tax-scraping): her 2027 return filed on Papers on 1 February 2028 with her money in a CD, $1,700.39 owed to the IRS, due 18 April 2028 at 11:59 PM. tax.file's unpaid branch (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1566) sets collection 0 and calls nextNotice (:389-393), which schedules from sim.now: CP501 on 7 March 2028 ('Notice CP501: $1,700.39 on your 2027 return; you still owe it, with the interest and penalty since.') and CP503 on 11 April, both before the due date, when no interest or penalty had run; CP504 on 16 May and LT11 on 20 June 2028, so the levy came 17 July, 90 days after the due date. No CP14 is ever sent: the first letter is a reminder. The same from-now count is in resumeCollection (:603-612, a plan refused before the due date) and endPlan (:631, a plan ended before it), and armCollection (:1165-1182) arms a save opened with a balance and no letter the same way; a save from before the fix holds its premature letter pending. Connecticut's side counts from max(now, its due date) since 2026-10-15 (statetax.ts:392-401): its bill came 18 May 2028, 30 days after the due date, and nothing before it.
rows.decisions: (1) nextNotice counts each step from the later of now and the return's due date, so no reminder, notice of intent or final notice precedes the due date, wherever collection is put on the calendar (filing, a plan refused or ended, a save opened). (2) tax.file sends the IRS's bill, Notice CP14, when it leaves a balance the bank couldn't pay and no plan takes it: on a return filed early it names the due date and says nothing is added before it; filed on or after the due date it gives what's owed with the penalty and interest charged. SLATE assesses at filing, so the CP14 is dated then (the IRS's own date is the Monday of the third week after posting: SLATE's simplification, said). (3) armCollection moves a letter that a save from before 2026-10-16 holds pending before its earliest lawful day (the due date plus its step's wait) to that day, once. (4) The guide, the tutorial's sentence and Papers' fine print say the bill comes at filing and the letters from the due date. (5) The tests that counted from an early filing are corrected: evidence-g17's journey files on the due date itself (where filing and the due date agree, so its 35th to 140th days after filing still hold); the federal lien test counts from the due date; scope-taxpapers' LT11 date and amount move to the IRS's lawful sequence, the title corrected and the audit's citation of it with it.
rows.changes: nextNotice counts each step's wait from the later of now and the due date, so no CP501, CP503, CP504 or LT11 precedes the due date, whether collection is put on the calendar at filing, after a plan refused or ended, or on opening a save.; The IRS's bill, Notice CP14, sent at filing when the bank can't pay the IRS's part and no plan takes it: the due date named on an early return, the penalties and interest on a late one; built from COLLECTION and RETURN's own figures.; Older-save compatibility: a pending IRS letter earlier than the due date plus its step's wait is moved there on opening (armCollection, run by loadSave).

Explain valid constraints and show the next legitimate action'); tax.md item 2: a control the screen draws that no valid state enables, or whose words promise what SLATE doesn't do, is corrected. Connecticut releases a lien once the tax it secures is paid (Conn. Gen. rows.reads: src/ui/components/LienPanels.tsx:66-72 draws, on every state lien, the line 'Filed in error, it’s withdrawn on request: …' and the button Ask For Its Withdrawal As Filed In Error, disabled with lienDisputeRefusal's reason (statetax.ts:726-731). lienInError (statetax.ts:718-724) is true only for a lien filed on a state's assessment that the taxpayer's own return later replaced (sd.replacedAt) with a balance no more than the tax paid before the lien was filed. For Connecticut, the only state a life files in, it never holds: a payment goes to the penalty and interest before the tax (12-39h), the lien is filed only while something is owed (stateLienStep, :629-640), and DRS's assessment of a non-filer is the return's own figure (assessStateNonFiler, :825-849), which the return replacing it repeats. Played on 2026-10-15 (tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts) on both of a student's Connecticut liens: drawn shut, the command refused. So the screen draws a control no valid Connecticut state enables, beside words promising a withdrawal.
rows.decisions: Draw the button, and the words that a lien filed in error is withdrawn on request, only on a lien the engine finds was filed in error (lienDisputeRefusal undefined), or show the request's own standing once asked (Asked To Be Withdrawn, Withdrawn, from LienFacts). On any other lien say what's true instead: it secured tax owed when it was filed, so it's released once that's paid, and Ask For Its Release is the next step. The command and its refusals stay (a guard: the command can be sent without the screen). The guide's taxes.lien entry says the button shows only on a lien filed in error.

rows.preconditions: ORS 305.992 and OAR 150-305-0068 (waived on written request before full payment or within a year after: 70% filed before any notice, 50% after a demand, 25% after an assessment), as content/statetax.ts carries them. A penalty already paid and then waived is an overpayment the department credits to what's owed or refunds (SLATE's reading of ORS 314.415's refunds and credits; the waiver's own text says nothing of a part already paid).
rows.reads: Unreachable: only Oregon charges it (content/statetax.ts, us-or threeYear) and every life files in Connecticut (played: tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts). Retained engine at 25% only (tests/liens-and-arrangements.test.ts:259). By reading (statetax.ts:1035): with the year still owing, the waived amount comes off the penalty owed, held at nothing, so a waiver larger than the penalty still owed (Oregon takes a payment to the penalty first, content/statetax.ts us-or order) drops the excess: the taxpayer's payment toward a penalty since waived is lost. Unconfirmed until a test reproduces it.
rows.decisions: Keep it. FIXTURE tests for the 70% and 50% shares (their own return before any notice; after a non-filer's letter), each through the command. Reproduce the excess: a part paid to the penalty first, then the waiver; if the excess is dropped, fix it: what was paid toward a penalty since waived comes off the year's interest and tax still owed, and the rest is refunded to the bank.

rows.preconditions: Each issuer's own rule for where the applicant is. A US citizen in the US renews by mail on Form DS-82 for $130 where the most recent passport was issued within the last 15 years, at 16 or older, valid for 10 years, never reported lost or stolen and undamaged (travel.state.gov 'Renew Your Passport by Mail', read 2026-10-16 through search; fee $130 in State's fee chart 'Updated October 2026', read through search 2026-10-16); otherwise Form DS-11, $130 and the $35 acceptance fee. A British national in the US applies from overseas: £116.50 online (gov.uk 'New fees for passport applications', published 18 March 2026, effective 8 April 2026, read 2026-10-16), and can't use the urgent Fast Track service ('You cannot use this service if you’re outside the UK', gov.uk/get-a-passport-urgently, read 2026-10-16). rows.reads: documents.apply_passport (documents.ts:314-331) charges every applicant the office's domestic fee (passportTerms, :411-414) and offers its expedite (:417-424), wherever they apply from. Every life is in New Haven, so a citizen of any other country applies from abroad: a London-born student pressing Renew It is charged the UK's £102 domestic fee and offered Renew It Faster, the UK's Fast Track (£192, 7 days), which isn't sold outside the UK; Papers shows the office's 'From abroad' text beside it, which says £116.50 (Documents.tsx:132) — the screen contradicts the charge. A US citizen renewing pays $165 (DS-11's $130 + $35) where DS-82 is $130. Loss: documents.report_lost (:333-349) cancels it; no replacement path besides applying again (correct: a lost passport is replaced by a new application). rows.preconditions: On a close, a German current account owes its regularly charged monthly fee only pro rata to the end of the contract (BGB § 675h(3)); on a cancellation in the cooling-off period, Wertersatz for the service given up to the withdrawal (§ 357b(2)), on the contract's price. The months already ended in the quarter are owed whole (each was served whole); the closing month's share by the days the account was open in it, through the closing day, of the month's days, in exact cents; nothing is refunded where nothing was paid ahead. Balanced ledger entries. The amount and its explanation shown before the player presses Close It or Cancel It. Month boundaries, leap years, the closing date, insufficient funds, a repeated attempt, save and load, and twins in one jump and day by day.
rows.reads: settleFees (src/engine/systems/banking.ts:521-530) and closingFeesOf (:543-545) charge the quarter so far (feesDue) and the whole of this month's fee (feeFor at the month's start), whatever day the account closes. Reproduced (scratchpad banking/base/tests/probe-banking.test.ts, run 2026-10-16): a Berlin-raised student keeping Deutsche Bank, at Yale from 24 August 2026, presses Close It on her AktivKonto on Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 9 AM and is charged “Closing fees: AktivKonto” −690 (€6.90), where 14 of October's 31 days are €3.12. Nothing on Your Banks or Your Accounts Over Time says what closing charges before it's pressed: the line under Close It (src/ui/bank/BankMoves.tsx:163) says only a refusal, and Cancel It's (src/ui/bank/BankAccountLife.tsx:116) says “less the fees it owes” without the figure. Fees collected ahead: none at a German bank in SLATE: feeFor's monthly fee accrues at each month's end into feesDue and posts at the quarter's closing (banking.ts:629-642), so every fee posted is for a month already served.
rows.decisions: One breakdown in banking.ts (closingFeesDue): the quarter's months kept (feesDue, and feesDueHeld in the bank's money), and this month's share: feeFor's figure (in the bank's own money first where the account is kept in another), times the days the account was open in the month through the closing day (from its opening day where it opened that month), over the month's days, rounded half up to the cent in integers; none once the month's end has accrued the month (a close after 11 PM on its last day). settleFees and closingFeesOf read it, so Close It's, Cancel It's and the bank's own close's refusals and charges are one figure. Its words (closingFeesWords) under Close It on Your Banks and under Cancel It, before either is pressed. The guide's Another Bank and Keeping An Account entries say it. Tests in tests/remaining-09-banking.test.ts, played on a Berlin-raised student keeping Deutsche Bank: the figure on the screen, pressed, posted once, the ledger balanced, a reload, twins jump and day by day, the month's first day, its last before and after the month's end, a quarter's end, February in 2027 and 2028, insufficient funds then paid in, a second press. The three tests the audit cites change with dated comments and new titles, recorded in docs/verification/pipeline/inputs/renames.json.

question.what: Whether the twelve rows reached only through a life living abroad or in another state (the eight bank rows, tax.catch_up_state_plan, tax.lien_dispute, tax.request_waiver), and tax.amend, which nothing in scope reaches, stay Unresolved, counted against completion, or move to Deferred Scope.
question.evidence: The bank-rows probe (110 lives, every bank abroad SLATE has research on) reached none of the six bank commands; Connecticut is the only state a life files in, and its plan, liens and penalties don’t reach the three state rows; no writer changes a filed year. Each row’s engine is tested on labelled fixtures (its acceptance.engine).
options: Keep them Unresolved: the denominator holds 12 rows no current player reaches, and completion is reported short by them (the page’s 95% stays under 100% for them alone).
Move them to Deferred Scope, as health.prepay was: nothing that works is hidden, the engine and its fixture tests stay, and the rows leave the denominator with their four parts kept.
For tax.amend alone, add an in-scope event that changes a filed year (a corrected W-2 for a year’s work-study), which would make it reachable; a product choice, since no source says Yale issues one.
question.recommended: Move the eleven reachable only through a removed system to Deferred Scope, since the owner removed the travel that reached them and brief 09 bars restoring it; keep tax.amend Unresolved until the owner says whether a corrected W-2 belongs in the game.

rows.reads: SchoolWorkspace.tsx:576-577 (CoursesPanel) says “{passed} of {all} courses passed so far.” and, with nothing failed or incomplete, “Only the terms to come stand between you and the degree.” whatever the standing; with something failed it says a year “can be repeated, below” to a student who has left. Reproduced 2026-10-16 (probe screens.probe.ts, seed js-g1, Ada Cole born in New York, wealthy family, the coursework prepared each midnight (TEST SETUP), played to 2 June 2029): Standing Graduated, and the tab says “58 of 58 courses passed so far. Only the terms to come stand between you and the degree.”, “In the casting pool.” (SchoolWorkspace.tsx:165), and Attendance, Growth and Coursework “This Term” with “90% is the floor”, “half its pace is the floor”, “half of 3 or more is short” (SchoolWorkspace.tsx:158-160), an evaluation that won't come. Its Casting tab draws “Not Cast Yet: The chair casts every student each term from the first spring…” (SchoolWorkspace.tsx:466-472) and its Coursework tab “Work Set: Nothing set yet: each course sets its work at a meeting…” (CourseworkPane.tsx:66).
rows.decisions: Say, once the School has ended, what is so: the degree conferred on its date with every course passed; or the way it ended and what was left unpassed, with no repeat offered. Drop “so far” and “In the casting pool.” for a student who has left; the term's three figures read as the last term's, their floors in the past tense; Not Cast Yet and Nothing Set Yet give way to what's so (no more casting; no work set, the School over). A student still at school keeps every sentence as it was.
rows.changes: Once the School has ended (schoolEnded): Courses And The Degree says how it ended (the degree conferred and its day; the withdrawal, dismissal or degree not recommended, with what wasn’t passed and no way on), drops “so far”; a course left in the middle reads Not Finished and isn’t listed with the term’s meetings; the three figures read Last Term with their floors in the past; “In the casting pool.” goes; Casting draws No Casting Ahead; Coursework says nothing is set because the School is over.

rows.preconditions: A payment to Yale draws on the primary current account and then the easy-access savings at its bank (banking.s7.school, leave.ts:772, Yale Student Accounts' payment options); unpaid by its due date, a financial hold and $125 a month to $375 a term (Bulletin; leave.ts:809); the hold stops registration (Bulletin p.184; leave.ts:1215-1222); paid, it lifts (leave.ts:793-806). Each step validated, said, and kept through a reload, one jump against small steps alike.
rows.reads: Played 2026-10-16 (probes p1-leave-hold.ts and p1b-return.ts, seed jy-1, Modest family, born in New York): a personal leave from 27 January 2027 returns $7,600.25 of the spring's living scholarship to the Yale account, due 26 February; Affiliate cover, $8,950.00, is bought from Chase Total Checking; $100.00 paid; the hold comes on 26 February with $125.00 and grows to the $375.00 cap; the return term, Spring Term 2028, begins with the hold and registration is refused in its words; paid from the bank, the hold lifts and registration is taken. Under it, the term's living scholarship is paid to the bank in full (“$14,093.64 is in your Chase Total Checking”) while $7,875.25 stays owed on the Yale account and the hold stands: see journeys.d-aid-past-balance. The savings branch was tested only on a charge put on the account by hand (tests/remaining-banking.test.ts banking.s7.school, TEST SETUP).
rows.decisions: Play it with no hand-set charge: the aid returned on a played leave, the player's own move of most of the current account into savings (bank.transfer), Affiliate cover bought drawing on both, the hold and its fees by the clock, the return, the refusal, the payment, registration, the term's classes counting; twins in one jump and in six-hour steps across the leave; reloads at each boundary.

rows.preconditions: A withdrawal after the fifteenth day of classes keeps Yale Health thirty days (Bulletin 2026–27 p.174; health.ts:263); enrollment opens 60 days before an expected loss and 60 days after it (45 CFR 155.420(c)); Medicaid (HUSKY D) at any time on a month's income; an F-1 student has fifteen days' grace and then no marketplace (45 CFR 155.305(a)(1)); the year's return reads what was paid and covered.
rows.reads: Played 2026-10-16 (probe p2-withdraw.ts): seed jw-1, Modest, born in New York, withdrew 5 October 2026 at noon: “Yale Health covers you for thirty days more.”; Enroll offers HUSKY D at once; uncovered from 4 November; on 1 December “Your Health Cover Ended: You’re uncovered from November 4, 2026. You have 60 days to enroll in the marketplace.” (journeys.d-cover-ended-notice); HUSKY D enrolled 2 December starts 1 January 2027, and a doctor's visit on 3 December is billed $183.98 uninsured (journeys.d-medicaid-start). Seed jw-2, born in London, F-1: out of status on 20 October, the marketplace refused in its words, the cover-ended notice says so, the 2026 return late with a refund waiting.
rows.decisions: Play both lives through the clock, with reloads at the withdrawal, the loss of cover and the enrollment; assert each notice's words and each refusal; one jump against six-hour steps from the withdrawal to February.

rows.preconditions: Connecticut's Uniform Policy Manual § 1560.10: “The beginning date of assistance for Medicaid may be one of the following: A. the first day of the first, second or third month immediately preceding the month in which the Department receives a signed application when all non-procedural eligibility requirements are met and covered medical services are received at any time during that particular month; or B. the first day of the month of application when all non-procedural eligibility requirements are met during that month” (as quoted in a DSS Office of Legal Counsel hearing decision, portal.ct.gov omel_2016_765192.pdf, read 2026-10-16; 42 CFR 435.915(a), (b)). From 1 January 2027 the retroactive months are one for expansion adults: 42 USC 1396a(a)(34) as Pub. L. 119-21 § 71112(a) amends it, “(A) in the case of an individual who is eligible for medical assistance … described in subclause (VIII) of section 1902(a)(10)(A)(i), in or after the month before the month in which the individual made application … if such individual was (or upon application would have been) eligible for such assistance at the time such care and services were furnished”, (B) the second month before for any other; § 71112(d), applications “made (or deemed to be made) on or after the first day of the first quarter beginning after December 31, 2026” (govinfo.gov, PLAW-119publ21, the statute's own text, read 2026-10-16).

rows.decisions: (Follow-up of 2026-10-16, the coordinator: implement.) HUSKY D enrolled or approved starts on the first day of the month of application (UPM § 1560.10(B)), care billed since priced again (repriceCare). Then the retroactive months (§ 1560.10(A)): the first, second or third month before the application month where she was eligible then and covered care was received in it; for an application on or after 1 January 2027, the month before only for HUSKY D's group (Pub. L. 119-21 § 71112(a), (d): 42 USC 1396a(a)(34)(A), 'furnished in or after the month before the month in which the individual made application', read in the statute's own text at govinfo.gov). Every hand-worked date the change moves worked again from the rule, with dated comments and renames (renames.json), tests/remaining-09-hardship.test.ts included. What SLATE can't read for a retroactive month recorded exactly.

No test's code or assertion changes.
rows.changes: tests/setup/ended-life.ts, loaded for every test file by vitest.config.ts’s setupFiles, wraps Simulation.prototype.advanceTo: on a life whose meta.endedAt is set, each call asked to move the clock past now is counted, and the millionth in a row throws an Error naming the player, the death’s time and age and the count; any other call (a live life, a target not later than now) resets the count, and every call goes through to the real advanceTo, which on an ended life returns at once with the clock where it stopped. rows.reads: tools/interpretation.ts builds both ST6 specialists as actor({…three at 85/75/75…}, fill(235)) with fill = (600 − n) / 8, and actor() reads every ability not named at fill: 9 abilities are left, not 8, so each specialist's total is 235 + 9 × 45.625 = 645.6 against the even actor's 600 (12 × 50), 45.6 over. ST6 as written compares a specialist with itself, so its budget moves little; ST6′'s 26 of 42 (brief 09) compared a 645.6 budget with a 600 one. ST3's voice-and-body specialist ((600 − 170) / 10 over 10 left) and ag-baseline's specialists ((600 − 85) / 11 over 11 left) total 600.
rows.decisions: Print each profile's budget with every result; fix fill to (600 − n) / 9 with a dated comment saying what it did; measure ST6 as written and ST6′ both ways (old fill and corrected) so what the defect changed is a figure.

The School's performance call holds 150 minutes (systems/school.ts:2713), the Rep's 180 (2740, 3437, 2749, and 1586 for a night on call), the Cabaret's 90 (3607) and the Summer Cabaret's 150 (3685), whatever the play.

Where a listing gives no interval's length, 20 minutes, the RSC's and the Globe's, said as SLATE's reading.

rows.goal: W5 Breaks recover, once: an interval recovers a bounded share of the drain for what follows it; that recovery isn't credited again (the clock's rest during the interval, the night's sleep).
rows.entry: src/engine/systems/workload.ts (new); src/engine/content/workload.ts (new)
rows.preconditions: Brief 10 section 4 ("Accounts for recovery without double-counting it"); criteria.md W5.
rows.reads: No night has a break: the drain grows by position alone (systems/piece.ts:331-341).
rows.decisions: At each break A is multiplied by 1 - R x min(1, minutes / 20); the energy after reads W, the work done, not A, so the break isn't credited there; the clock charges waking hours through the interval as it does any (it never recovers energy awake, systems/life.ts applyElapsedWellbeing), and sleep is untouched.

rows.goal: W6 Elapsed time and fatigue applied once: the call holds the clock for the running time and its calls, once; its fatigue is applied once; a save and a load during or after the evening applies neither again.
rows.entry: src/engine/systems/school.ts; src/engine/index.ts (ONCE_ON_OPENING)
rows.preconditions: Brief 10 section 4 ("Applies elapsed time and fatigue once"); criteria.md W6.
rows.reads: The calls hold 150, 180, 90 or 150 minutes whatever the play (above); the fatigue is taken once at the curtain by the call's handler (systems/school.ts:3500 and the others); the waking hours of the call are charged by the clock (systems/life.ts chargeWakingHours).
rows.decisions: Each performance call booked for its production's running time plus the curtain call; the on-call hold and the run-through likewise; the energy taken once in the call's handler from the night's own workload; a save from before has its pending performance calls re-timed once on opening where nothing else the player must attend overlaps the new span.

rows.goal: W7 Segments sum to the whole: the drain and fatigue of a performance judged in its units equal the same performance processed whole, under 1e-9.
rows.entry: src/engine/systems/workload.ts (new); src/engine/systems/piece.ts
rows.preconditions: Brief 10 section 4 ("Handles segmented performances consistently with the same performance processed as a whole"); criteria.md W7.
rows.reads: The drain is sampled at each segment's start by position (systems/piece.ts:331-341): a piece processed whole, one segment, has no drain at all, while its units do.
rows.decisions: Each segment's drain is the mean of the drain over its span of the running, integrated exactly (A is piecewise linear; the bound's min integrated in closed form); the energy's per-segment shares are each segment's share of the workload.

decision.question: Should (e2.3), (e3.3) and (e4)'s margins be read on the abilities' part alone, both takes judged with the scene's grain at nothing, with the margins as played kept as the record; and should (e3.5) on stage be read on the size counterparts' own opportunities (varied on every actor) with their 10 gains reported, rather than the gains alone?
decision.evidence: As in results; acting/st6r2-13-e.json (verdict.e2, verdict.e3, atNoGrain, and per actor extraNotOver005 and otherSideNotBehind), and the trace of romantic_drama-2/plan above.
decision.recommendation: Accept both and close ST6-R2.e. The specialist advantage the owner asked for is what the specialist's abilities do, and the grain at nothing isolates exactly that, one input held for both actors; it held on every piece for every one of the fourteen comparison actors. It was added to the measure beside the verdict after the informing actors were checked and before the fresh ones ran (0ddfaed1), and the fresh run met it with no exception; it was seen after the informing check, so it's proposed, not adopted. On stage, size's room for actors leaning toward restraint is 1 to 10 pieces each, so a quarter of 10 gained pieces is 2 from one play; the counterparts' own opportunities there meet the floors. Keeping the clause as written leaves ST6-R2.e not met.
